A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Orbit Diffusion research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including identification of reorganized material and the removed Appendix D.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendices C–D report original synthetic, molecular, crystal, and protein experiments, plus empirical estimator analyses.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C retain original synthetic experiments and Orbit Diffusion evaluations for molecular conformers, crystal structures, and protein generation.

M1.justification: Appendix C.1.3 revises the reported flow-matching estimator: v2 applies orbit estimation to both conditional expectations for x0 and x1, whereas v4 uses a single prior sample x0 and orbit estimation for x1. The core orbit-weighted procedure and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the synthetic reflection task, GEOM-QM9 conformer generation, Perov-5/MP-20 crystal prediction with and without text conditioning, and protein generation. The removed diagnostic uses a subset of the retained molecular data, without introducing distinct task or population coverage.

E2.justification: Benchmark comparator membership in Tables 1–9 is unchanged. Removing Appendix D.2 eliminates Figure 11's comparison against the full-support importance-sampling reference estimator constructed using 80,000 samples.

E3.justification: Removing Appendix D eliminates evaluations across training checkpoints and 100/1,000/10,000 orbit samples, together with the fixed-noisy-input bias protocol. Retained benchmark splits, metrics, and evaluation sample counts remain unchanged. The newly specified ETFlow checkpoint initialization does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V4 removes Appendix D.1's sensitivity analysis across noise levels, training epochs, and orbit sample counts, and D.2's bias–variance study using eight molecular conformers. This substantially reduces direct estimator diagnostics, although the main efficiency, convergence, gradient-variance, and equivariance analyses remain.

E5.justification: The removed Appendix D.2 documented eight random-seed repetitions of target estimation and averaging over ten noisy inputs per noise level. Synthetic mean/standard-deviation reporting and three-repeat CSP medians remain. V4's checklist newly acknowledges incomplete error-bar reporting because training costs limit repeated runs.

E6.justification: V2 Figures 9 and 11's detailed variance trends and intermediate-noise bias findings disappear, removing a substantial set of estimator results. Tables 2–9 retain their values. Table 1 changes the RMSD multiplier from 10^-6 to 10^-5 without changing its entries, a tenfold absolute-value revision rather than a demonstrated performance change.

T1.justification: V2's Theorem 2 establishes orbit-target equivariance. V4 adds equality between the exact orbit-weighted loss gradient and the ideal gradient, with a new unbiasedness proof in Appendix B.4. This substantially extends the theoretical guarantee; the other principal proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims: variance reduction through Rao–Blackwellization, compatibility with equivariant and non-equivariant models, equivariant minimizers, computational efficiency, and the same benchmark performance claims. The conclusion's rewriting does not materially change their scope.

C2.justification: V2 interprets orbit restriction as trading small bias for reduced variance and warns about missing contributions outside the sampled orbit. V4 instead establishes unbiasedness for the exact orbit loss and removes those bias qualifications. Its limitations emphasize proposal flexibility and sample-count accuracy–cost trade-offs.

D1.justification: V4 adds a project-code link and explicitly identifies public-checkpoint fine-tuning for ETFlow, which v2 did not clearly document for OrbDiff. Section 4.5 also adds approximately 40 MB of extra memory per GPU against approximately 54 GB total usage. Most existing implementation and hardware details remain.

R1.justification: Section 3.1 adds citations to Kingma et al. (2021), Nichol and Dhariwal (2021), and Xu et al. (2023) concerning diffusion-training variance. The main related-work discussion and Appendix A retain their previous research positioning.

P1.justification: Section 3 is substantially rewritten into four numbered subsections separating motivation, gradient estimation, conditional expectation, and practical implementation. Limitations become a standalone section, Appendix D is removed, and a NeurIPS checklist is added. These materially reorganize the narrative.

P2.justification: V4 removes Appendix D's three figures, revises the appendix crystal galleries, and adds a combined crystal gallery to the main text. Figure 1 is relocated within the method section, and theorem displays are revised. Most benchmark table structures and principal result plots remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V4 adds a useful exact-orbit unbiasedness proof, clearer method organization, and implementation/access information. However, it removes empirical bias and sensitivity diagnostics and associated qualifications while Algorithm 1 still uses finite self-normalized importance sampling. The new exact-integral guarantee does not resolve the finite estimator's behavior, and the benchmark scores otherwise remain unchanged. These gains and losses do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
